name: Description
descr: The content half of a goods: what a buyer reads about it - the names, the codes, the texts, the seo, the clan and the characteristics standing on it. The very fields the Description window of the program writes back, the price among them, though the money proper belongs to the Price tool. The right is for_frame, given out in the program on the sections a goods hangs in, so only goods hanging in a section of yours are reached here.

commands.name: CmdTopic
commands.descr:
Walks the goods of the sections named - the plain way to see what stands where. Searching by the columns of the map is CmdQuery.

Name the sections in topic_id, and topic_sub takes the whole branch under each of them; the Catalog tool answers the tree to pick them from. A section this person may not price is walked past, whatever the call names.

The goods come by id, and so does every page of them: a walk of many pages loses none and says none twice. Where a goods stands and at what place comes with it, in the rows of topic_store - sort by that if the order of the shop is what is wanted.

A goods hanging in several of the sections walked is answered once. The answer is the one CmdQuery gives: the goods, the sections they hang in, their characteristics, the objects tied to them - and found, the whole count of what stands there, whatever the page asked for.

params.name: topic_id
params.descr: the sections to walk, and nothing outside them

params.name: topic_sub
params.descr: true - the whole branch under every section named is walked with it

params.name: limit
params.descr: how many goods of the ones standing there to answer with; found says how many there are in all, so a page is chosen knowing the size

params.name: offset
params.descr: how many of the goods found to step over before this page - 100 takes the second page of a hundred

commands.name: CmdQuery
commands.descr:
Finds the goods by a query written as json and answers them with everything that hangs on them - the goods, the sections they hang in, their characteristics, the objects tied to them.

ASKED FOR NOTHING - an empty query, or none at all - it answers its own signature instead: every table with every column and its type, and what may be asked of each. Nothing outside that list is taken, so a first call asks for it and the ones after are built by it.

THE SHAPE. A query starts from the root table of the sign and holds a list of conditions. A list is an AND, always. Four things may stand in it:
a condition - {"field": "price", "op": "between", "value": [1000, 5000]};
an or - {"or": [ ..., ... ]};
a not - {"not": ...}, of one condition or of one nested table;
a nested table - {"topic_store": [ ... ]}, which means THERE IS such a row: every condition inside it holds on one and the same row. A table goes one level deep only, and only a table the sign marks nest.

THE SECTIONS are a nested table like any other: {"topic_store": [{"field": "topic_id", "op": "in", "value": [9, 10]}]}. The sections are named as they are - a whole branch is named section by section, and the Catalog tool answers the tree to build such a list from.

NOTHING STANDS BESIDE THE ROOT TABLE. The page is a field of the call - limit and offset - and the goods come by id, page after page, so a walk of many pages loses none and says none twice. Sorting them any other way is done by whoever reads the answer. Whatever the page, the answer carries found - the whole count of what matched - so the size of a search is known without pulling it.

THE OPERATIONS come from the type of the column, and the sign names them: eq, in, between, ge, le for numbers, eq, between, ge, le for days, eq, in, like for words, eq for flags. between takes two values, in takes a list, the rest take one. like looks for a part of the text anywhere in it.

AN EXAMPLE of the whole thing:
{"store": [
  {"field": "no_visible", "op": "eq", "value": false},
  {"field": "price", "op": "between", "value": [1000, 5000]},
  {"or": [ {"field": "status_key", "op": "in", "value": ["kExist", "kExistOrder"]},
            {"field": "brand_id", "op": "in", "value": [1, 2]} ]},
  {"topic_store": [ {"field": "topic_id", "op": "in", "value": [9, 10, 11]} ]},
  {"store_info": [ {"field": "info_id", "op": "eq", "value": 1},
                   {"field": "value_id", "op": "eq", "value": 2} ]},
  {"not": {"store_set": [ {"field": "obj_key", "op": "eq", "value": "kStore" } ]}}
]}

The goods of a list of ids are asked for the same way: {"store": [ {"field": "id", "op": "in", "value": [25, 26]} ]}.

The right stands beside the query and is not part of it: only the goods hanging in a section this person may describe are ever met, whatever the query says. The place a goods keeps in a section is answered here but never written - the Place tool shapes that, and what a goods costs belongs to Price.

params.name: query
params.descr: the query itself, as the shape above; left out or empty, the command answers what may be named in one

params.name: limit
params.descr: how many goods of the ones found to answer with; found says how many there are in all, so a page is chosen knowing the size

params.name: offset
params.descr: how many of the goods found to step over before this page - 100 takes the second page of a hundred

commands.name: CmdAdd
commands.descr: Adds a goods and hangs it in the section at once - a goods hanging nowhere is seen by the Lost tool alone. Every column of the half may come in the same call; the days left out are stamped now, and a fresh goods is born hidden, out of stock and plain. The section must be yours to describe.

params.descr: id of the section to hang it in

commands.name: CmdInfoAdd
commands.descr: Sets a characteristic on goods: one row of store_info on each of them, and a characteristic holding several values at once takes a row for each. The characteristic itself comes from the Attributes tool - a value of its list goes by value_id, a number by value_dec, a text of your own by value_txt.

params.name: store_id
params.descr: id of the goods, or several of them

params.name: info_id
params.descr: id of the characteristic - the Attributes tool answers them

params.name: value_id
params.descr: id of the value of that characteristic, when it keeps a list of them

params.name: value_dec
params.descr: the number, when the characteristic keeps numbers

params.name: value_txt
params.descr: the text, when the characteristic keeps its own words

commands.name: CmdInfoUpdate
commands.descr: Changes the columns given of the rows of store_info; a row keeps whatever the call leaves out. CmdTopic answers the rows of a goods with their ids.

params.name: id
params.descr: id of the row of store_info, or several of them

params.name: store_id
params.descr: moves the row to another goods; that goods is weighed by the same right

params.name: info_id
params.descr: moves the row to another characteristic of the shop

params.name: value_id
params.descr: id of the value of that characteristic, when it keeps a list of them

params.name: value_dec
params.descr: the number, when the characteristic keeps numbers

params.name: value_txt
params.descr: the text, when the characteristic keeps its own words

commands.name: CmdInfoRemove
commands.descr: Deletes the rows of store_info by id. The characteristic itself stays in the store, and the goods keeps the other ones standing on it.

params.name: id
params.descr: id of the row of store_info, or several of them

commands.name: CmdSetAdd
commands.descr: Ties another object of the store to goods: one row of store_set on each of them. obj_key says what is tied - a goods or a section - and kind_key what the tie means; the storefront reads that: accessories, a kit, a section to send to.

params.name: store_id
params.descr: id of the goods, or several of them

params.name: obj_key
params.descr: a value of STORE_SET_OBJ_KEY: kGoods ties a goods, kTopic ties a section

params.name: kind_key
params.descr: a value of STORE_SET_KIND_KEY - what kind of tie it is, the owner names them

params.name: elem_id
params.descr: id of the object being tied - a goods or a section, by obj_key

params.name: params
params.descr: the parameters of the tie, as the storefront reads them

params.name: comment
params.descr: a note for the people of the shop

params.name: pos
params.descr: the place in the list; left out, it goes to the end

commands.name: CmdClannNew
commands.descr: Makes a fresh clan over the goods named and answers its number: a clan holds the variants of one thing - the sizes of a shirt, the colours of a cup - and the storefront shows them as one card. root names the goods that leads it, and left out the first of the named leads. A goods already in another clan changes clans. CmdUpdate with clann puts one more goods into a clan that stands.

params.name: id
params.descr: id of the goods, or several of them

params.name: root
params.descr: id of the one that leads the clan; the first of the list when left out
